translations.translatedText: # Monday 17.1.2022 (radio)
Corona infections. Corona test device. Honour violence. Winter storm. Weather forecast.
## Corona figures
![THL sign on Mannerheimintie in Helsinki.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11358354)
Open image viewer
The Institute for Health and Welfare, THL, collects Finland's corona figures. Photo: Tiina Jutila / Yle
Over 22,000 new corona infections have been confirmed in Finland. Monday's figures include infections from the weekend.
There are also 29 new corona deaths in Finland. In total, over 1,700 Finns have died because of corona.
About 700 corona patients are in hospital care.
## Corona test device

![Managing director Pekka Rissanen of DSA Oy blows into a corona tester.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5755,h_3237,x_1,y_178/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-90285961e562a303823/1642423185)
Open image viewer
A new device measures from breath air whether a person has a corona infection. Photo: Antti Eintola / Yle
A new device for corona testing has been developed in Finland. The developers say that they now have permission to sell the device.

The device can be used to do a corona test from breath air. First the user blows into the device. The device measures the breath air and sends the data via a mobile phone to a cloud service. There the measurement data are examined, and the result comes to the mobile phone. Everything takes less than a minute.
The device is intended for health care professionals. For example, occupational health care, school health care and dental care may be able to start using the device.
## Preventing honour violence

![Project coordinator Merja Kankare (left) and project worker Doaa Al-Shmes of Setlementti Tampere ry, from the Kunniaksi project.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_4000,h_2250,x_0,y_561/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-90199861e162329ba60/1642161471)
Open image viewer
Merja Kankare (left) and Doaa Al-Shmes work in the Kunniaksi project. Photo: Jarkko Vuolle / Yle
In Tampere, an attempt is made to prevent honour violence with the Kunniaksi project.
Kunniaksi project worker Doaa Al-Shmes says that honour violence can also be psychological violence. For example, a man does not let his wife out.
In the Kunniaksi project, men who have committed or are planning honour violence are talked to.
Doaa Al-Shmes says that the reason for honour violence may be that the family has not yet adapted to Finnish society. Finland's different culture may be frightening.

Clients can also talk with Doaa Al-Shmes in Arabic. Through their own mother tongue, immigrants receive information about Finnish society and culture. It helps them adapt to Finland, Doaa Al-Shmes says.
## Winter storm
![Stairs being shovelled.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_4000,h_2250,x_0,y_418/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-90260561e5295288ce0/1642408357)
Open image viewer
The stairs of the Triplan shopping centre were cleared of snow on Monday. Photo: Benjamin Suomela / Yle
There was a winter storm in Finland on Monday.
A strong wind blew across Finland. The wind cut electricity in different parts of the country, and many homes were without electricity for a while.
In the Lapland fells there was almost a hurricane. The wind speed was as high as 39 metres per second.
Driving conditions have also been poor. Pedestrians have also been warned about slippery streets.
## The weather
![weather map](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-12274788)
Open image viewer
On Tuesday snowfall comes to Lapland, elsewhere it is dry.
Cloud cover increases in the western part of the country, but in the east the sun still shines.
On Tuesday there is frost of 1 to 10 degrees, but the wind adds to the biting cold. During the day the temperature rises above zero in the western part of the country.
On Wednesday the weather warms. The temperature is a little above zero in almost the whole country.
